title: Option strategies III: covered call, protective put, collar, butterfly and condor
objectives: Compute maximum profit, loss and breakevens for covered call, protective put and butterfly.
Choose between income, protection and range-bound strategies.
body_md:
## Stock-plus-option strategies

| Strategy | Build | Aim |
|---|---|---|
| **Covered call** | Own stock, sell a call | Income; caps the upside |
| **Protective put** | Own stock, buy a put | Insurance against a fall |
| **Collar** | Own stock, buy a put, sell a call | Cheap protection, capped upside |

Covered call: stock 500, sell 520 call at 8. Max profit = (520 − 500) + 8 = **28**. Breakeven = 500 − 8 = **492**.

Protective put: stock 500, buy 480 put at 10. Max loss = (500 − 480) + 10 = **30**. Breakeven = 500 + 10 = **510**.

## Range-bound strategies

**Long call butterfly:** buy 100 call at 12, sell two 110 calls at 7, buy 120 call at 4. Net debit = 12 + 4 − 14 = **2**.
Max profit = (110 − 100) − 2 = **8** at 110. Max loss = 2. Breakevens: **102** and **118**.

**Iron condor:** sell an out-of-the-money call and put, buy further wings for protection. Collects net premium if the index stays inside a range; loss is capped by the wings.

**Ratio spread:** unequal numbers of long and short options; can carry unlimited risk on one side.

## Choosing

Bullish and income: covered call. Worried about a fall: protective put or collar. Expect low movement: butterfly or condor.

> **Exam tip:** Covered call breakeven is stock price minus premium received.
example: Own a stock at 500 and sell a 520 call for 8: if the stock closes at 540 the gain is 20 + 8 = 28, not 48.
say: A covered call earns income but gives up gains above the strike.
A protective put is insurance, so it has a cost.
never: A covered call has no downside.
A condor can never lose money.
